title: typedef-add-spec
description: INPUT of `dmtool -m <model> typedef add --id <id> <spec.json>` — the reusable type definition's config: a `kind` + its per-kind block, the SAME per-kind shape a field's type takes in `field-add` (so an ENUM type-def declares `enum.values`, a restricted STRING declares `string.pattern`/`length`, etc.). A type definition carries ONLY a type — no group/name/requiredness/label/metadata (those are field/element concerns; set a type-def's descriptions/annotations with `meta <id>`), so any such key is rejected with RK_UNKNOWN_ARG. The simpler `typedef add --id <id> --kind <K>` flag covers a bare easy kind; this spec covers the rich ENUM/restricted kinds. Validated against the real kernel before writing. (`--kind` and this spec are mutually exclusive.)

kind.description: STRING | NUMBER | DATE | TIME | DATETIME | DATERANGE | DATEFRAGMENT | BOOLEAN | CONFIRM | ENUM | CUSTOM

minLength.description: minimum character length. seeAlso: the Length operator — the rule-level way to bound length (`operators Length`)

pattern.description: anchored Java Pattern; REQUIRES patternMessage (a pattern and its error message must be set together — patternMessages alone is rejected). Authoring first requires Java syntax, then the kernel 30.8.x restrictions: the finite A12K-30 blacklist (possessive quantifiers, (?<… / (?>…), \A \G \Z \z \a \e \p \Q \E, nested unescaped [) plus the typed/full-model \P rejection. Passing them does not prove JavaScript portability. seeAlso: the PatternViolated/PatternMatched operators — the rule-level alternative (`operators PatternViolated`)

patternMessage.description: the error text shown when the pattern fails; REQUIRED whenever `pattern` is set (the base message, applied to every declared locale unless patternMessages overrides a locale). A `pattern` without it is rejected: 'a pattern and its error message must be set together'

patternMessages.description: OPTIONAL per-locale override ON TOP of patternMessage, { "<locale>": "<text>" }; wins over patternMessage for that locale (patternMessage stays the required base/fallback for the rest) — the string sibling of an enum's per-locale invalid-value text, so a bilingual model can localize the pattern error. It does NOT stand alone: supply patternMessage too, or the field is rejected

noValueValidation.description: skip the kernel's per-value validation (each stored value) (for base64 blobs / attachment content etc.); the kernel REQUIRES lineBreaks alongside it (MVK_STRING_TYPE_NO_VAL_AND_NO_LINE_BREAK), so set lineBreaks:true too or the field is rejected. A raw-type field's VALUE is then unusable in rules/computations — presence checks only; the sole value-shaped exception, a whole-condition Length(f) > c, is a max-length declaration the kernel eliminates (see `dmtool diagnostics MVK_INVALID_RAW_TYPE`). Read back via `field read` under string.noValueValidation

suggestions.description: per-locale hint list, { "<locale>": ["…"] }; validated against the field's own pattern

maxFractionalDigits.description: the decimal scale; together they bound the fraction-digit range

min.description: minimum value (decimal as a string). seeAlso: the LessThan/GreaterThan comparison operators — rule-level bounds

values.description: ≥1 { value, labels? } — stored value + optional per-locale labels. seeAlso: FieldValueIncludedInValueList / FieldValueNotIncludedInValueList — the rule-level way to (dis)allow a value set

categories.description: named classifications; each has values[] aligned 1:1 with the enum values. seeAlso: the EnumCategory operator (`operators EnumCategory`) — reads a value's category in a rule

description.description: optional editor-level note for the category (the kernel core ignores it; preserved for the editor's Category table)

values.description: values aligned 1:1 with the enum values

sValue.description: the stored-token S-value — the model-owned INDEX default: when this enum is a repeatable group's index field, full validation transiently supplies this token for a nonmandatory index that is absent/present-empty on the parent's only row (partial validation instead silently suppresses that cell). Must name one of the declared values (checked at authoring — the kernel stages it into evaluation unvalidated)

invalidValueMessage.description: error text for an out-of-domain value — one text expanded across ALL declared locales (the shorthand)

errorMessages.description: per-locale invalid-value error text, { "<locale>": "<text>" } — wins over invalidValueMessage; must cover every declared locale (omit both to use the kernel default)

format.description: a LOWERCASE Java date pattern from a fixed allowed set (independent of locale): yyyy-MM-dd or dd.MM.yyyy. The A12 editor's UPPERCASE labels (YYYY-MM-DD) are display labels, NOT valid format values. Default yyyy-MM-dd.
a Java time pattern; the kernel requires the FULL HH:mm:ss — HH:mm (no seconds) is rejected. Default HH:mm:ss.
a LOWERCASE Java date+time pattern; verify the exact accepted form with a `field add --dry-run`.

a LOWERCASE Java date pattern for both endpoints, from a fixed allowed set (independent of locale/conditionLanguage). VERIFIED (format, separator) pairs: dd.MM.yyyy with -, and yyyy-MM-dd with /. The editor's UPPERCASE preset labels (YYYY-MM-DD, MM/MM, …) are display labels, NOT valid format values.

separator.description: the single-character range separator PAIRED with the format: - for dd.MM.yyyy, / for yyyy-MM-dd. A spaced ' - ' or a mismatched separator is rejected ('The date range format is invalid').

format.description: a LOWERCASE Java partial-date pattern (a date that isn't a full calendar date) — VERIFIED: MM, yyyy, yyyy-MM, MM-dd. The A12 editor's UPPERCASE labels (YYYY, YYYY-MM) are display labels — use lowercase yyyy.
